action: As the lottery sellers ask, Takarakuji users must reset their password to log in, and anyone who used the same ID and password on other sites should change it there too.
date_note: Impress Watch says the unauthorised logins were on 4 November (Security NEXT: 4 and 5 November) and that the selling prefectures and designated cities announced the scope on 13 November; dated by that announcement.
exec: Reused passwords let attackers into thousands of customer accounts at a national lottery service and change the passwords.
org: National Local Government Lottery Administration Council (Takarakuji)
plain: Attackers used leaked passwords to log into lottery websites and apps in Japan. They got into thousands of accounts and changed most of the passwords.
summary: Japan's Takarakuji lottery websites and apps were hit by a password list attack. Impress Watch says the selling prefectures and designated cities announced on 13 November that attackers logged into 4,436 accounts on 4 November and changed the password on 4,133; Security NEXT gives 4 and 5 November. Names, birth dates, purchase history and partial account and card numbers may have been seen. No purchases or payout changes were confirmed.
title: Japan's Takarakuji lottery accounts hit by password list attack

validation.note: Impress Watch (13 November) and Security NEXT (17 November) are independent publishers giving the same counts, 4,436 accounts logged into and 4,133 passwords changed (Security NEXT as read by the first researcher and the review of 19 November; Impress Watch read by the follow-up of 22 November). The sellers' own notice was not read.

review.note: Compared title, date, 4,436 and 4,133 figures and evidence quotes, exposed data, attack type against Impress Watch and Security NEXT

evidence.quote: 不正なログインの被害を受けた利用者のアカウント数は4,436。
このうち4,133名についてはパスワードの変更も行なわれたとしている。
